plays.name: Price and the royalty ladder
plays.gate: none, but test it, do not roll it out
plays.why: Each dollar of list price is 60c of headroom per click. $9.99 affords a $0.24 click, $12.99 affords $0.42, and the cheapest click we ever won cost $0.50. This is the whole game in one line.
plays.judge: CVR held vs matched controls over 30 days

plays.name: The $9.99 cliff and the Kindle window
plays.why: Print pays 50% below $9.99 and 60% at or above. Kindle pays 70% ONLY between $2.99 and $9.99 and 35% outside. Opposite shapes; applying one to the other loses money both ways.
plays.judge: royalty per sale, read off KDP

plays.name: Review velocity
plays.why: 29 of 43 advertised books have zero reviews. Reviews set conversion, conversion sets what a click is worth, and that sets every bid. Also the gate on every attack play. Three 5 star reviews take a 2.0 to 4.25.
plays.judge: CVR before and after crossing 5 reviews

plays.name: The organic flywheel
plays.why: A sale bought at a loss still moves rank, and rank is not rented. This is the honest argument for tolerating Stage 1 tuition.
plays.judge: BSR improving while ad spend stays flat

plays.name: Concentration over breadth
plays.why: Tranches of 8 to 10, never all at once. Spreading thin means every book gets too few clicks to say anything. Statistical power, not thrift.
plays.judge: clicks per book reaching the 40 click verdict

plays.name: Own-ASIN product targeting
plays.why: Your own detail pages currently show competitors' ads. A reader on your page already chose your subject: the cheapest qualified traffic there is. The highest-value defensive play we are not running.
plays.judge: share of our own carousel, NOT ACOS. Accept up to 1.5x breakeven

plays.name: Negative keywords
plays.why: Three tiers: category noise (book bag, bookends, book nook), proven losers at 12+ clicks and no order, and self-competition. That last one is forgotten most: a term promoted to Exact must be negated in the campaign that found it or we pay twice for one click.

plays.name: Negative ASINs
plays.why: Stop showing on pages of books that beat us on rating, reviews or price. We are paying for the privilege of losing a side-by-side comparison.

plays.name: Placement discipline
plays.gate: earn it back only in Stage 3
plays.why: Final CPC is bid x dynamic x placement. 89 of 92 campaigns carried +70% at top of search, so a $0.55 bid really bid $0.94 where most clicks land.

plays.name: Dynamic bidding, down only
plays.why: Up-and-down hands Amazon permission to bid above our ceiling on its own judgement. Our ceiling is arithmetic, not a preference.
plays.judge: default on every campaign we create

plays.name: The wallet guard
plays.why: Warns at 80% of the monthly ceiling and pauses every enabled campaign at 100%. The only play that cannot be undone by a mistake in another play.

plays.name: One edition per book
plays.why: A paperback and its Kindle share reviews but bid against each other in the same auction, splitting the sales signal and raising the price of a click we would have won anyway.
plays.judge: enforced in activate and in the tranche picker

plays.name: Competitor ASIN targeting
plays.gate: ALL THREE: our rating >= theirs, our reviews >= half theirs, our price <= theirs
plays.why: The shopper sees both books side by side. Win that comparison and it is superb; lose it and we paid for them to choose the other book. Today exactly one title clears the gate.
plays.judge: reviews first, then attack. In that order, always

plays.name: Category targeting with a price refinement
plays.gate: none, and that is the point
plays.why: Target the category filtered to books priced ABOVE ours. Every shopper who sees us is looking at something more expensive, so we are the value option by construction. The best attack that does not need reviews.
plays.judge: cap the budget hard, category targets are broad

plays.name: Search-term harvesting
plays.why: The ONLY play that compounds. Every other play rents traffic; this turns spend into a permanent asset. A phrase proven to convert is free intelligence for every book we launch after it.

plays.name: Head-term conquesting
plays.gate: royalty per sale would need to roughly triple
plays.why: 'childrens books' costs about $1.01 a click. Our affordable click is $0.24. Four times our ceiling before we start.

ladder.means: we are simply paying too much per click

ladder.means: budget or bid limited, which is a good problem
ladder.fix: scale one lever at a time: budget +20-30% OR bid +10-15%, never both
